newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-SPANISH SET SAIL FOR FRENCH TITLE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SPANISH SET SAIL FOR FRENCH TITLE.

text.p: The Spanish sailed into the French Open on Tuesday and laid siege to the grand slam event.
Led by former-champions Sergi Bruguera and Arantxa Sanchez Vicario, no fewer than 16 of 25 Spaniards entered in the tournament cruised safely into the second round.
Long renowned for their clay court prowess, the Spanish have been particularly dominant on the slow surface this season.

Having won four of the seven European clay court events and the World Team Cup ahead of the French Open, there has been talk of a new Spanish reign similar to 1994 when Spaniards occupied three-of-four places in the men's and women's finals, claiming both titles.
One of the few hurdles facing the Spaniards, however, comes in the shape of other Spaniards. Of the nine who failed to advance, three were taken out by their own compatriots
Of the eight seeded Spaniards, Alberto Berasategui, the losing half of an all-Spanish final in 1994, has been the only one to make a first round exit.
"All the Spanish are very strong," said 10th seed Felix Mantilla, "Maybe there will be four Spanish in the semifinals. I hope so."
The idea may not be so far-fetched.
Top seeded Spanish man, number eight Alex Corretja, the winner of two events this season and the finalist in two others, is regarded as the most serious threat.

But right behind him is Australian Open finalist Carlos Moya, the ninth seed, who advanced at the expense of compatriot Alberto Martin and could oust another of his countrymen in the second round when he meets Albert Portas.

Two-time champion Sergi Bruguera, winner of back-to-back French titles in 1993 and 1994, meanwhile appears recovered from the ankle problems that plagued him last season and could be in the hunt for a third title.
Of the seven women seeing action in the opening round, five are through cleanly.

Sanchez Vicario, the winner in 1994 and a finalist the last two years, will be hoping a return to the site of her greatest triumph will turn around what has been a disappointing season which has seen the former world number one drop to number six, her lowest ranking since 1990.
Conchita Martinez, the 1994 Wimbledon champion, will be looking to get past the semifinals where her bid for the French title has stalled the last three years.
The Spaniards will certainly present considerable second round hurdles for two American title hopes.
World number one Pete Sampras, making a bid for the only grand slam crown to elude him, has to meet Francisco Clavet, ranked a respectable number 29 in the world.
The match is one of the centre court highlights on Wednesday. Clavet reached the quarter-finals at last year's tournament before losing to eventual champion Yevgeny Kafelnikov.

On the women's side, Martinez meets Chanda Rubin, also on centre court. In the 1995 French Open, Rubin famously fought off nine match points and overcame a third set deficit of 0-5, love-40 to upset Jana Novotna and reach the quarter-finals.
